summary: A HashSet stores each item once and checks membership in O(1) on average by using hash codes. Your own class needs both equals() and hashCode() for a set to treat equal objects as duplicates.
notes: hashCode() returns Objects.hash(studentId) because it uses the same field as equals(). Equal objects must have equal hash codes.
equals takes Object, not Student. Writing equals(Student other) overloads instead of overrides, and HashSet never calls it.
retainAll() changes the set to keep only items also in the other set: the intersection.
pitfall: Overriding equals() without hashCode() compiles with no error, but HashSet.contains() usually returns false for an equal object because it looks in the wrong bucket.
